decisions.rationale: Verified at f18bccaf. Loop 1 (for the shared E1/F5 Problems-label finding) added EDITOR.check in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js. It re-kinds every adapter 'limit' whose message is not on a phrase list as kind 'error' (shown as 'Error'). Replayed with the adapter's check() and that exact regex: SELECT * FROM public.students; ... ORDER BY name COLLATE "C"; UPDATE students SET (city, name) = (...); SELECT DATE '2024-01-01'; and ORDER BY student_id USING > all become Error. These are valid PostgreSQL per the cited SELECT, UPDATE and lexical-structure documentation (not executed on a server). The adapter's generic messages ('could not read the statement near', 'Expected ... near', 'The statement ends too early') cannot tell a real mistake from unsupported valid syntax. The rule in DESIGN.md (Editor workspace, Problems: "An error the real language certainly raises is danger. An unsupported construct ('limit') is warning") and in authoring/evidence/python/python-fundamentals/lesson-editor/README.md (adapter contract: kind "error" is reserved for code the real language certainly rejects) therefore forbids this relabelling. The fix also missed its own target: the typo 'SELEC * FROM students;' still comes back as a limit. Remedy (a), REVERT: remove the loop-1 EDITOR.check override (and its comment), restoring the 8a7daa17 behaviour where every adapter 'limit' shows as 'Not in this practice editor'. That matches the unchanged LIMITS item 4 in build.mjs ("Anything else is marked Not in this practice editor: a limit of this page, not a sign that your SQL is wrong") and the page footers again. Run gating is unaffected either way: the shell blocks Run on any non-hint problem, and onSqlRun's 'did not use up a try' path is unchanged. Keep the separate loop-1 E5 wording in onSqlRun ('a missing comma or semicolon is often at the end of the line before it'); it does not depend on the override. This REOPENS the shared E1/F5 Problems-label finding on all eight pages (C2E-AGG-03, C2E-ANTI-03, C2E-FILT-06, C2E-GRP-04, C2E-NULL-02, C2E-JOIN-05, C2E-IUD-02 (graded high), C2E-SEED-01): real mistakes are again labelled 'Not in this practice editor', which the LIMITS text says is not a sign of wrong SQL. Record it as a recipe finding for the sql-practice adapter in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/engine.js. The adapter should give kind 'error' only to statements it can prove malformed (an unclosed quote or bracket, a statement ending after WHERE/AND) and give generic parse failures neutral wording ('could not read this; check for a typo, or it may be SQL this editor does not support'). Until then, this is an open item for the task owner. Remedy (b), leave, is rejected: it tells learners valid SQL is wrong, in breach of the adapter contract.
